papers.title: Meromorphic approximation of holomorphic maps into algebraically elliptic projective varieties
papers.abstract: We show that holomorphic maps from a neighborhood of a compact set in a Stein space to an algebraically elliptic smooth projective variety can be approximated by meromorphic maps, provided that the map extends continuously to the whole space and the compact set is convex with respect to a submonoid of the Picard group. The proof uses algebraic sprays and their polynomial lifts to affine cones, which we call conic lifts. Rational sprays, which generalize algebraic sprays, extend the result to maps avoiding the exceptional set of a rational spray. We also show that, for smooth projective varieties, the existence of an algebraic spray which is dominating at some point is a birational invariant.

papers.title: A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $\Xi$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods
papers.abstract: We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $\Xi$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Zero-action resonance reduces to rationality of two real period ratios. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|\kappa|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $\kappa$. Fixed-point irrationality and exact Picard rank remain open. The heat tangent differs from the matched fixed-exponent isomonodromic direction, but admits a local moving-exponent curve lift. Separately, a reciprocal-head canopy certificate combined with published finite-RH and rectangular time-barrier verifications bounds the de Bruijn--Newman constant by $\Lambda\le433/2500=0.1732$ without a QRH assumption. These local arithmetic and global analytic results share a phase--transverse bridge; no equivalence between core nonresonance and RH is asserted.

papers.title: Envelopes of Horospheres and Weingarten Surfaces in Hyperbolic 3-Space
papers.abstract: We derive basic differential geometric formulae for surfaces in hyperbolic space represented as envelopes of horospheres. The dual notion of parallel hypersurfaces is also studied. The representation is applied to prove existence and regularity theorems for Weingarten surfaces in H^3, which satisfy (1-a)K = a(2-H), for an a < 0, and have a specified boundary curve at infinity. These surfaces are shown to be closely connected to conformal mappings of domains in S^2 into the unit disk and provide Riemannian interpretations for some conformal invariants associated to such mappings. This paper was originally written in 1984, before I learned to use TeX, and was typed by one of the secretaries in the Princeton Math Department. It was more or less, my first original work after my dissertation. For some reason, I was not able to get this paper published in a timely manner. The results and perspective in this paper have proved to be useful to a variety of people, some of whom asked me to render the article into TeX and post it to the arXiv. I had been seriously thinking about doing this, when Martin Bridgeman sent me a transcription of my original article into TeX. I am extremely grateful to him for the effort he has put into this project. The paper is now formatted in a more or less modern AMS-article style, but for lots of additional punctuation, a few corrections and some minor stylistic changes, the content has been largely reproduced as it originally was. Remarks about the 'state-of-the-art' in hyperbolic geometry are obviously way out of date, as there has been enormous progress in many aspects of this still rich subject.

papers.title: Oka Geometry of Complex Six-Spheres
papers.abstract: Alp\"oge constructed a complex structure on $S^6$ through a torus fibration with exactly three special fibres. We prove that every member of the associated admissible period family is Oka and that the family projection over each relatively compact parameter disc is an Oka map. The Oka property survives the deletion or simultaneous blow-up of any finite set of distinct points in any member. Blowing up a single point therefore produces an Oka complex manifold diffeomorphic, but not biholomorphic, to $\mathbb{P}^3$. The proofs combine explicit cyclic coverings with analytic extension and the invariance of the Oka property under holomorphic coverings.

papers.title: The Calabi-Yau and Sullivan conjectures for minimal surfaces with symmetries
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite group acting on a connected open Riemann surface \(X\) by holomorphic automorphisms and acting on a Euclidean space \(\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge 3\), by orthogonal transformations. In a previous paper, the second author gave a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a \(G\)-equivariant conformal minimal immersion \(F:X\to\mathbb R^n\), and he asked whether such \(F\) can be chosen to be a proper map. Assuming that this condition holds, we give an affirmative answer when \(X\) is a bordered Riemann surface and \(G\) acts freely on the boundary of \(X\). This contributes to the Sullivan conjecture concerning the existence of proper hyperbolic minimal surfaces in \(\mathbb R^3\) of finite topology. Under the same conditions, we also construct a \(G\)-equivariant proper conformal minimal immersion of \(X\) to the unit ball of \(\mathbb R^n\) which is complete in the induced metric, thereby opening a new direction in the Calabi--Yau theory regarding the study of complete bounded minimal surfaces. Analogous results hold for null curves in \(\mathbb C^n\).

papers.title: A Kallin's lemma for polynomials with exponents in a compact convex set and local approximation
papers.abstract: Let $S\subset\Bbb R_+^n$ be compact and convex with $0\in S$, and let $\mathcal{P}^S$ be the algebra spanned by monomials with exponents in $\bigcup_{m\ge0}(mS\cap\Bbb N_0^n)$. We define the associated polynomial hull and prove a Kallin lemma for the union of two sets convex with respect to this algebra. A weighted approximation lemma then shows that, under a sector or ray condition, two admissible monomials generate exactly the functions of the unrestricted algebra that are constant on a specified zero fibre. Applications include an exact density criterion for mixed monomials, a transfer principle for relative perturbations, and density and hull computations on stars of totally real discs.

papers.title: Absolute moments of GH distribution
papers.abstract: In this work, we focus on deriving the absolute moments of the general ized hyperbolic (GH) distribution via its mean-variance mixture structure. Conditioning on the GIG mixing variable reduces the problem to Gaussian moment calculations and known GIG power moments, avoiding direct integration with Bessel functions. The variance gamma (VG), normal inverse Gaussian (NIG), hyperbolic, Normal, and Student t distributions emerge as natural special or limiting cases of the generalized hyperbolic family. This approach offers a substantially simpler and more transparent derivation, facilitating both implementation and verification.
